title: Writeback-aware coalescer and deferred-decode unblocking for paged KV
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem: In production workloads with long conversational histories and mixed short/long requests we observe periodic prefill stalls and decode jitter caused by eviction/writeback work contending with decode kernels. The current eviction path performs eager fragment reclamation and immediate writeback for dirty KV pages which increases tail latency when GPU decode throughput is saturated.

Proposal: Implement a writeback-aware coalescer that batches and defers non-critical writebacks and performs background consolidation of small dirty fragments, coupled with a deferred-decode unblocking mechanism. The coalescer will: (1) maintain lightweight liveness and reuse probability metadata per fragment; (2) classify writebacks as high/low urgency based on tenant SLA, fragment reuse score, and memory pressure; (3) schedule low-urgency writebacks during identified low-decode-utilization windows (micro-idle), and coalesce contiguous fragments to amortize PCIe/CP DMA costs. The deferred-decode-unblocking logic will: (A) temporarily re-route decode work to alternative kernel variants with lower interference sensitivity when a large writeback batch is in-flight; (B) apply small, bounded decode preemption windows instead of a full stall; and (C) orchestrate a short-lived in-GPU soft-reservation that pins hot fragments to avoid repeated migration during a single request.

Why this is different: Existing eviction heuristics are immediate and fragment-scoped which increases IO amplification. Our approach reduces writeback frequency by coalescing fragments and leverages runtime kernel-selection signals to avoid worst-case interference scenarios. This targets tail-latency improvement without increasing steady-state memory usage significantly.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark (long-conversation mix) shows 25-40% reduction in 99th-percentile prefill latency under heavy writeback pressure
No more than 5% increase in average token-cost across evaluated workloads
Automated correctness test proving all dirty fragments reach durable storage within configured urgency bounds
Can be toggled via runtime feature flag and rolled back with no loss of cache integrity
milestones: Integrate kernel-selection hinting into runtime (owner: Kernel-Team) - 2026-03-22
Full rollout gated on perf signals - 2026-04-02
notes: Trade-offs: Deferring writebacks increases window of potential data loss if not durably replicated; mitigated by tiered urgency and strict max-defer timeout per fragment.
We need to coordinate with the telemetry team to add a 'writeback_inflight' signal and kernel-interference metric for feedback loop.
Coalescing contiguous fragments may require minor reshaping of shard layout which is backward-compatible at page-level but needs careful padding to avoid cross-tenant contamination.
progress_updates: 2026-02-23: Spike completed comparing coalescing granularities (4KB, 16KB, 64KB) — 16KB shows best amortization vs reuse loss.
2026-02-28: Prototype scheduler implemented; initial synthetic perf tests show decode interference drops ~18% when background writebacks align with micro-idle windows.
2026-03-05: Kernel team accepted a lightweight hint API (KERNEL_HINT_AVOID_IF_WRITEBACK) for temporary routing to robust kernel variants.
2026-03-10: Added safety timeout for deferred writebacks (default 1.2s); running extended soak on internal Dedicated cluster
risks: If urgency classification is too permissive, we may violate tenant durability expectations — requires conservative defaults.
Kernel hinting adds complexity to routing; mis-tuned policies could shift latency elsewhere (e.g., CPU-side bottlenecks).
Coalescing may increase memory pressure momentarily while waiting to emit larger writebacks; monitor and cap coalescer queue depth.
testing_plan: Unit tests for coalescer state machine and urgency classifier
Integration test simulating mixed workload (chatty short requests + long generation) with deterministic seed to reproduce prefill stalls
Chaos test: randomly drop background writeback network packets to verify durability timeouts trigger immediate fallback
Performance metrics dashboard: 99th/95th decode latency, writeback throughput, kernel-interference score
release_notes: Feature gated by runtime flag 'kv.writeback_coalescer'. Default off for hosted API; enabled for Dedicated private canaries. Documentation and rollback playbook in Confluence.
